summary: This work demonstrates scalable alternating-bias-assisted annealing (ABAA) for transmon frequency tuning on 150 mm wafers, achieving $\sigma = 0.50 \pm 0.05\%$ junction resistance precision and $98.8\%$ component-level yield through multi-channel parallel tuning. Implementation on the Rigetti Cepheus-1-36Q quantum processor achieves empirical frequency targeting precision of $\sigma \sim 30$ MHz in both $f_{01}^{\mathrm{max}}$ and qubit-qubit detuning, directly enabling high two-qubit gate fidelities.
motivation: Post-fabrication Josephson junction tuning is essential to compensate for inherent nanometer-scale variations in junction area and barrier thickness that limit as-fabricated targeting to $\pm 3\%$ resistance spread, yet scaling ABAA to foundry production requires demonstrating throughput, yield, and stability across wafer-scale processes.
method: Multi-channel simultaneous ABAA tuning was implemented using high-density probe cards and source-measure units; junction breakdown voltage (BDV) was characterized as a critical process control parameter via phase diagrams correlating BDV, annealing voltage amplitude, and short probability; temporal stability was monitored over 14 weeks post-tuning in nitrogen-purged storage; Hamiltonian targeting was validated on a modular 36-qubit processor with frequency prediction based on room-temperature resistance measurements.
result: Parallel ABAA achieves $30$-fold throughput gain at 108 channels while maintaining targeting precision; wafer-median $f_{01}^{\mathrm{max}}$ spread improved from $294 \pm 106$ MHz (as-fabricated) to $9 \pm 12$ MHz (post-ABAA prediction) and measured $132 \pm 30$ MHz after cooldown; qubit-qubit detuning targeting error reduced to $\mu \pm \sigma = 1 \pm 32$ MHz experimentally, with higher two-qubit gate fidelities observed when detunings match design specifications.
